acidic.name: Agricultural Lime (CaCO3)
acidic.notes: Most cost-effective. Slow-acting. Also adds calcium.

acidic.name: Hydrated Lime (Ca(OH)2)
acidic.notes: Fast-acting but more expensive. For quick pH boost.

alkaline.name: Gypsum (CaSO4·2H2O)
alkaline.notes: Doesn't lower pH directly; improves soil structure to reduce lime effects

alkaline.name: Elemental Sulfur
alkaline.application_method: Broadcast; soil microbes oxidize S → H2SO4
alkaline.notes: Slow but effective. Most economical for long-term correction.

deficient.name: Urea (46% N)
deficient.application_method: Dissolve in water and apply at V4-V6 growth stage. Split application: 30% basal, 40% at boot, 30% late season.
deficient.application_timing: Split: 30% basal, 40% at V4-V6, 30% at boot
deficient.notes: Fast N source. Cheap. Apply with water to avoid volatilization loss.

deficient.name: DAP (Diammonium Phosphate, 18% N + 46% P2O5)
deficient.application_method: Broadcast basal application at sowing, incorporate 10 cm deep with soil.
deficient.notes: Dual nutrient boost. Excellent for N+P co-deficiency.

deficient.name: FYM (Farm Yard Manure, ~0.5% N)
deficient.notes: Also improves soil texture, water retention, organic matter. Slow-release.

deficient.name: Single Super Phosphate (SSP, 16% P2O5)
deficient.application_method: Broadcast basal application at sowing, incorporate 10 cm deep into soil.
deficient.notes: Cost-effective. Also adds sulfur (12% S). Slow dissolution in high-pH soils.

deficient.name: DAP (Diammonium Phosphate, 46% P2O5 + 18% N)
deficient.notes: High P concentration. Excellent for P+N co-deficiency.

deficient.name: Bone Meal (organic, ~11% P2O5)
deficient.notes: Slow-release. Also adds calcium. Excellent for long-term P build-up.

deficient.name: Muriate of Potash (MOP, KCl, 60% K2O)
deficient.application_timing: Basal at sowing or split 50-50 basal+boot
deficient.notes: Most common. However, high chloride—avoid for tobacco/potato/grapes if possible.

deficient.name: Potassium Sulfate (SOP, 48% K2O + 18% S)
deficient.notes: Premium option. No chloride. Also adds sulfur. Higher cost.

deficient.name: Wood Ash (K2O ~4%, + Ca, Mg)
deficient.notes: Slow K release. Also raises pH (use cautiously in alkaline soils). Free if available.

deficient.name: FYM (Farm Yard Manure, ~2% OM)
deficient.notes: Improves water holding, aeration, microbial activity. Cheap source if on-farm.

deficient.name: Compost (fully decomposed, ~3–5% OM)
deficient.notes: Faster nutrient release than FYM. Higher OM per ton. More expensive.

deficient.name: Green Manure (legume cover crop)
deficient.application_timing: Off-season. Plow in 4-6 weeks before main crop.
deficient.notes: Free nitrogen via legume fixation. Excellent for soil health. Requires planning.
